main_text.p: negativa ut liquet ex verbis Polycarpi mox descriptis, Polycarpus siquidem su-premos Ecclesiæ Philippensium rectores nuncupat Presbyteros, qui etiam Epi-scopi appellabantur, immò seipsum in Epistolæ inscriptione Presbyteri nomine insignit, saltem nihil aliud sonare viden-tur hæc inscriptionis verba, Polycarpus, & qui cum eo sunt Presbyteri: Nam si gradum Presbyteratu superiorem obtinuisset, à Presbyteris suis Episcopi nomenclaturâ se distinxisset, præterea Irenæus qui Po-lycarpi auditor fuerat, quique libros suos adversus hæreses XV. circiter post illius mortem annis scribebat, eum Beatum & & Apostolicum Presbyterum vocat apud Eustreb. lib.5. cap. 20. 3. non plane constat Epistolicum Ignatium gradus semper enumerare, vel de singularibus sui temporis ministris loqui, quoties Episcopos à Presbyteris adeo caste ac religiose secer-nit; nec quicquam causæ est cur celeber-rimus Ignatianorum vindex Episcopos demortuos & antiquiores, superstitibus & præsentibus opponat pag. 167. 178. Quasi Irenæo licitum fuerit illos Presby-teros appellare, hos verò nequaquam; Irenæus enim de Episcopis se antiquiori-bus non solùm ita loquitur, sed etiam de præsentibus ac superstitibus: Franciscus

page.notes: The first word reads "negativa" and the page opens mid-paragraph, so the paragraph is marked as continued. The reading "Eustreb." in the citation is a doubtful reading of "Eusebi" or "Eusteb." as printed; please check it against the scan. The ampersands before "Apostolicum" are printed as two different glyphs; both are given as "&". Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The page is printed in roman with the quoted words in italic.
